work_completed: AGENT-LOOP-002 T2 (doors and interior exits as explicit usable targets), asked for by Joshua 2026-10-18.
TaskAnchor.Link (new PortalLink record: target scene id, building index) marks doorway anchors; open-world door anchors link to SettlementBuilder.SceneIdFor(kind, index) and building index.

AnchorAffordances (TaskAnchor.cs) is the one rule set for perception and the ingress re-check: ordinary anchors keep their axis-derived sit/use; doorways afford use/approach/look_at by flag, never sit, and are never occupied. PerceptionBuilder and IntentIngress both call it, replacing the hand-mirrored NeedsAffordance.
PerceptionBuilder.VisiblePlaces extracted (engine-free) so the harness checks perception directly.

SceneAnchorSets (new, SceneAnchors.cs): per-scene anchor sets. Open world: the existing set. A loaded room: one exit anchor, id exit_<sceneId>, 1.6 m inside the doorway along the exit portal's inward axis, linking back to the open world through the room's own building. Rooms not yet loaded and unknown scenes have no anchors.
SceneCatalog.TryBuildingIndexFor: a room's id encodes its building (personal_4 is building 3), so the exit knows its origin without extra state.
AgentLoopDriver.AnchorsFor replaces the single Anchors list: perception and ingress ask with the avatar's scene; ResolveTarget checks the deciding avatar's scene anchors before scene node names.
WorldView exposes the shown interior's id and exit portal read-only (ShownInteriorSceneId, ShownInteriorExit); Main builds SceneAnchorSets from them.
AgentHarness: 20 new door/exit assertions covering the three T2 acceptance items.
decisions_made: The exit's origin building is derived from the room's scene id rather than recorded separately; SettlementBuilder gives each building its own id, so the id is the record.

Door anchors link to their building by index and SettlementBuilder.SceneIdFor, the same derivation the settlement uses for its portals, rather than reading WorldView's portal list (which would make the anchor builder depend on a live scene and break the harness).
Anchors are resolved before scene node names in ResolveTarget now, not in T5, because room exits are the first anchors inside interiors whose ids could collide with level node names.

handoff_record.next_agent_notes: T3 is next. Facts found in-engine that T3 must handle: (1) the home level's floor collision is at y = -4.01, four metres below the visible floor (the office level's is at 0.00), so only AvatarGround (y = 0) holds an avatar in a home; spawn-height ray casts there will find the wrong floor or AvatarGround. (2) WorldView.AddSocialExitDoorway hides UCX_Social_Wall_N after InteriorPhysicalBoundary already built collision from it, so the cafe's doorway is visual only; the academic doorway is also blocked about 0.1 m before the door plane. T3's design (stop at the exit anchor inside, engine places the avatar outside) does not need the doorways open. (3) With the loop on, OpenWorldBodiesLive keeps open-world bodies live and makes a shown interior display-only, so a placed avatar would have no room collision until T3 changes that split for the avatar's scene. (4) avatar.Anchors (the wander fallback) is still the open-world set; T3 must swap it to the room's set on entry. Exit anchors were probed against real collision in all four levels: the avatar capsule fits with no hits.
